listings.title: Jaisalkot Heritage Resort, Jaisalmer
listings.summary: The Jaisalkot resort by Girivar Hotel and Resort Private Limited is a completed 50-key heritage resort on a 15.26-acre converted site near Jaisalmer, Rajasthan. Offering a constructed area of 1,30,000 sq ft, the property includes four room categories and amenities such as a spa, swimming pool, and restaurant. The asset is available through a resolution plan under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, with India SME Asset Reconstruction Company Limited (ISARC) holding 100% creditor voting rights.
listings.body:
This investment opportunity centers on Girivar Hotel and Resort Private Limited's Jaisalkot Heritage Resort located off Sam Road near the Kuldhara turn in Village Manpia, Jaisalmer, Rajasthan. The completed heritage resort spans approximately 15.26 acres (61,738.93 sq m) of land that has been converted for hotel use, with a constructed area totaling 130,000 square feet. The built form is a palace-style single block arranged around courtyards over basement, ground, first, and second floors.

The resort comprises 50 air-conditioned rooms categorized into four types: 21 Kunwar rooms (368-407 sq ft), 15 Rawal suites (463-598 sq ft), 8 Maharani suites (687 sq ft), and 6 Maharawal suites (760-787 sq ft). Room features include central air conditioning, electronic safes, LED TVs, direct dial telephones, tea and coffee makers, minibars, and complimentary Wi-Fi. While the property lacks a lift, in-house parking is provided.

On-site facilities include a swimming pool, a constructed but not yet licensed bar area, a luxury spa, health club and gym, business centre, 24-hour front desk and room service, Suraman Mahal restaurant, Shatranj Lounge, and landscaped gardens.

Geographically, the resort is situated approximately 11-12 kilometers from Jaisalmer city centre, about 24 minutes by road from Jaisalmer Railway Station, and roughly 41 minutes by road from Jaisalmer Airport, which has limited connectivity. The major transport hub is Jodhpur, 280-285 kilometers away by road.

The land conversion to hotel use was approved by the District Collector in 2009, with documented chain of title dating from a registered sale deed in 2007 and subsequent approvals for tourism use. The approved site plan permits a floor area ratio (FAR) of 2.0; currently, the utilization is approximately 0.09 (less than 5% of the allowed FAR), including an approved extension for 28 additional keys. This presents potential for expanding accommodation subject to fresh regulatory approvals.

Key operating licenses in place include Rajasthan State Pollution Control Board consent valid until 2031 (orange category, 50 rooms), FSSAI state license for hotel and restaurant valid until 2029, formal tourism industry status granted in 2022, tourism project approval, and MSME registration as a micro enterprise. However, certain licenses remain outstanding, such as the bar license for the constructed bar area, fire NOC, occupancy certificate, hotel classification, and shops and establishments registration.

Fixed assets have a provisional valuation of approximately Rs. 25.62 crore, encompassing buildings, plant and equipment, furniture, electrical installations, computers, vehicles, and land at historical cost. Utilities comprise an 11 kV HT electricity connection (with fixed monthly charges payable even during closure), water supplied via external tankers, power backup through a 125 KVA diesel generator, oil-fired boiler, solar water heater, and a sewage treatment plant. Insurance coverage is current through July 2027.

The resort was operational until April 2026 but is currently closed pending insolvency resolution proceedings initiated in July 2026 under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code. The appointed Resolution Professional is managing the asset with a resolution plan submission deadline of 20 November 2026. India SME Asset Reconstruction Company Limited (ISARC) holds 100% creditor voting rights, being the sole secured creditor.

Financial performance between FY22-23 and FY24-25 shows peak revenue of Rs. 4.10 crore in FY23-24 with positive EBITDA only in that fiscal year; net losses were recorded annually. Tax attributes available to a prospective investor include unabsorbed depreciation of around Rs. 24.58 crore (with no time limit) and business loss carry forward of Rs. 0.12 crore (valid through AY 2031-32), collectively enhancing financial structuring possibilities.

This heritage resort investment presents a significant asset with substantial landholding and scope for expansion through unutilized approved FAR. The asset’s scale, core existing approvals, and single creditor committee structure simplify negotiation and acquisition. Given the unresolved insolvency proceedings and missing licenses, potential investors should conduct thorough due diligence, verify all approvals, and carefully evaluate operational restart requirements.

This asset stands as a distinctive heritage hospitality proposition in Jaisalmer with notable growth and repositioning potential subject to regulatory consent and capital commitment.

listings.title: Shirdi Hotel Development & Residential Plots
listings.summary: A five-level hotel structure occupies the principal parcel at Sai Niwara Township. Thirty adjoining residential plots complete a 5.15-acre holding on Shirdi–Pimpalwadi Road in Rui, Maharashtra.
listings.body:
## The hotel site

Plot 1 covers 12,757.65 sq m, approximately 3.15 acres. An existing ground-plus-four-storey structure gives the hotel development a physical starting point. The site photographs show the building in its shell condition. Commercial operations have yet to begin.

For a hotel developer, the opportunity is to shape the guest experience within that structure. The arrangement of rooms on the upper floors, the position of dining and reception at arrival level, and the movement of guests and service staff are all choices for the completion design.

## The residential plots

Alongside the hotel, Plots 2 to 31 comprise 30 residential plots covering 8,071.58 sq m, approximately 2.00 acres. They account for approximately 39% of the holding. The township schedule identifies each plot by number, giving the residential component a defined footprint within the larger site.

## Location and connections

The township lies in Rui, in Rahata taluka, on the Shirdi–Pimpalwadi Road. The project presentation places the Sai Baba Samadhi Mandir approximately 5.2 km from the site by road. It also gives indicative distances of 7.8 km to Sainagar Shirdi railway station and 18.6 km to Shirdi Airport.

For a hotel serving pilgrims, these connections matter at arrival and departure. Airport and station transfers can be planned alongside trips to the temple. Family room configurations, group dining and space for coach arrivals are practical choices for the hotel design.

## Property and transaction particulars

The project documents identify Trillion Real Estate and Properties (India) Private Limited as the owner of the hotel parcel and the 30 residential plots. The hotel is identified as Plot 1, Gat Nos. 303, 305, 308B and 312B/4/1. The two components together measure 20,829.23 sq m.

The project documents describe a corporate insolvency resolution process. The resolution professional’s current process documents govern participation, the transaction timetable and the assets included in a resolution proposal.

listings.title: Park Plaza Ludhiana
listings.summary: A 114-key city hotel on approximately 1.46 acres in Ludhiana, held by Majestic Hotels Limited and also identified as Majestic Park Plaza. Explore the asset through the applicable resolution process; current operating status and transaction terms require confirmation.
listings.body:
Park Plaza Ludhiana, also identified as Majestic Park Plaza in the supplied investor presentation, is one hotel asset held by Majestic Hotels Limited. It is located at Bhai Bala Chowk on Ferozepur Road, Ludhiana, Punjab. The source material reports 114 rooms on approximately 1.46 acres, with the land measurement to be reconciled against title and sanctioned records.

## The hotel and its operating footprint

The supplied material describes guest accommodation, food and beverage outlets, banquet halls and meeting facilities. These support a city-hotel proposition serving corporate travel, events and social functions. The documented built form includes two basement levels, a ground floor and ten upper floors.

## Room inventory and information period

The source presentation reports 77 operational rooms and 37 rooms requiring further review for refurbishment or possession matters, within the total inventory of 114. These are source-reported figures, not a confirmation of the hotel's current operating inventory.

The historical operating information includes monthly trading figures through October 2024. Current room availability, occupancy, revenue, possession and capital expenditure requirements must be confirmed before investment decisions.

## Operator agreement

The supplied presentation reports a Sarovar Hotels management agreement through 31 December 2028. The executed agreement, continuing validity, transfer provisions and operating obligations require review. This is an operator agreement, not the tenure of the underlying property.

## Transaction and next steps

The source material describes an investment through a resolution-plan process. The current process stage, eligibility, deadlines and approvals must be checked with the authorised parties. India Gully can coordinate the approved property information and the next disclosure step through the project data room.

The main diligence priorities are title and land measurement, possession and room recovery, current operational information, refurbishment requirements, and the applicable management and transaction documents.

perspectives.title: Apeejay’s 94% occupancy is not a city benchmark
perspectives.summary: Apeejay’s July to September 2026 occupancy covered only its eight owned hotels. Juniper’s room metrics for the same quarter excluded Bengaluru. Neither figure measures occupancy in a prospective acquisition’s local market.
perspectives.body:
## The portfolio figure and the city chart measure different things

Apeejay’s 94% occupancy for July to September 2026 covered eight owned hotels with 1,115 rooms, not all 43 operational hotels in its network. A separate nine-city chart puts Apeejay at 100% in Kolkata against an industry figure of 84%. In Indore, both figures were 68%. The chart labels the company series “ASPHL”, not “owned hotels”. It supports a company-to-industry comparison in each city, not a claim about the highest and lowest occupancy among the eight owned hotels.

## Juniper’s quarterly improvement excludes Bengaluru

For the same quarter, Juniper reported that occupancy rose from 72.3% to 74.7% year on year while average room rate rose from ₹10,599 to ₹11,514. Juniper excluded Bengaluru from both measures and from revenue per available room. By its November release, the company had announced the soft opening of the 238-room first phase of the Westin Bengaluru. The quarterly figures show that Juniper sold a greater share of available rooms at a higher average rate in the hotels it counted. They do not measure demand for the Bengaluru rooms.

## Why the distinction matters in a valuation

A buyer needs an occupancy assumption for the target hotel, not a ranking of operators. A hotel serving the same guests in the same city may be a better comparison than a portfolio under the same brand. Its stage of operation matters too: an established hotel can help a buyer assess demand once a new property is trading normally without telling the buyer how quickly it will get there.

## Build the comparison from room-nights

Ask the seller for room-nights sold and available by property and month. Which hotels compete for the target’s guests? When did rooms enter service, and how were temporary closures treated? For the hotels and months that fit, divide total room-nights sold by total room-nights available. That gives each available room-night equal weight rather than treating a small hotel’s occupancy percentage as equal to a large hotel’s. Check the room rates achieved over those same months before using the comparison to project revenue.

perspectives.title: A hospitality project starts with a better brief.
perspectives.summary: Connect the guest proposition, operating requirements and project budget before design decisions harden.
perspectives.body:
## Define the guest and the occasion

A hotel serving business travel, a leisure resort and a banquet-led property have different operating requirements. Set out the intended guest, stay pattern and role of rooms, food and beverage, events and other facilities.

## Bring operations into design

The design brief should address guest movement, service circulation, storage, kitchens, housekeeping and maintenance alongside the visible experience. Review these interfaces with the relevant design and operating professionals.

## Connect the budget to the programme

Separate building works, interiors, equipment, operating supplies and pre-opening requirements. Track responsibilities, dependencies and decision dates so that a late specification or approval does not become a surprise at handover.

## Treat opening as a workstream

Opening readiness includes staffing, training, operating procedures, supplies, systems and testing. Define acceptance criteria and the handover evidence required from each appointed party.
perspectives.image_alt: A hospitality project starts with a better brief.

perspectives.title: Compare specifications before comparing prices.
perspectives.summary: A useful procurement comparison makes inclusions, quantities and commercial terms visible.
perspectives.body:
## Keep the requirement identifiable

Assign each requirement a stable line reference. Record the intended use, specification, unit of measure and quantity. Preserve that reference through vendor responses, substitutions, approvals and orders.

## Distinguish a match from a substitution

A similar description does not necessarily represent the same product. Compare material, dimensions, capacity, finish, accessories, warranty and service scope. Identify deviations explicitly and obtain approval before treating alternatives as equivalent.

## Compare the complete commercial basis

Keep base price, taxes, freight, installation and other charges separately visible. Compare minimum quantities, lead times, payment terms and delivery locations alongside price. Mark unquoted lines rather than assigning assumed rates.

## Close the loop with an approval record

Record the selected specification, sample approval, commercial terms and delivery requirement. A change after selection should create a new version so the project team can identify what was ordered and why.

perspectives.title: What makes an asset ready for a serious conversation?
perspectives.summary: A clear brief and a consistent fact base give the transaction process a stronger starting point.
perspectives.body:
## Start with the decision

An owner considering a sale, a development partnership or refinancing is asking three different questions. Define the intended outcome, the time available and the constraints before preparing a presentation or beginning counterparty outreach.

## Build one consistent fact base

Bring the asset description, area measurements, ownership information, approvals, leases and financial records into a controlled information set. Separate a documented fact from a management estimate and an adviser’s assumption. Record the date and source of each important figure.

## Make the commercial case inspectable

Show how revenue, costs, capital expenditure and timing support the proposed transaction. Explain sensitivities and information gaps. A polished memorandum is most useful when the underlying assumptions can be followed.

## Sequence disclosure

An introductory teaser and a detailed diligence room serve different purposes. Agree what can be disclosed at each stage, who can receive it and how questions will be tracked. Specialist advisers should review matters within their respective scopes.
